You are a programming expert. 
        You will be provided with a patch used to fix a bug. 
        Based on the commit message and modifications in the patch, you need to analyze the root cause of the bug in detail. 

        Here is the patch content:
        From 65c4c7d850010049562e27c40639aba1d0526ead Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Bjoern Walk <bwalk@linux.vnet.ibm.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Feb 2016 10:19:51 +0100
Subject: [PATCH] qemu: cgroup: fix cgroup permission logic

Fix logic error introduced in commit d6c91b3c which essentially broke
starting any domain.

Signed-off-by: Bjoern Walk <bwalk@linux.vnet.ibm.com>
---
 src/qemu/qemu_cgroup.c | 2 +-
 1 file changed, 1 insertion(+), 1 deletion(-)

diff --git a/src/qemu/qemu_cgroup.c b/src/qemu/qemu_cgroup.c
index 53642a1c4b..f3c5fbb14e 100644
--- a/src/qemu/qemu_cgroup.c
+++ b/src/qemu/qemu_cgroup.c
@@ -65,7 +65,7 @@ qemuSetupImagePathCgroup(virDomainObjPtr vm,
     if (!virCgroupHasController(priv->cgroup, VIR_CGROUP_CONTROLLER_DEVICES))
         return 0;
 
-    if (readonly)
+    if (!readonly)
         perms |= VIR_CGROUP_DEVICE_WRITE;
 
     VIR_DEBUG("Allow path %s, perms: %s",
-- 
2.25.1


        
        Provide a response strictly in the following format:
        Root cause:<Root cause>

Root cause: The bug was caused by a logic error in the permission check for cgroup device access, specifically in the condition that determines whether to set write permissions. The original code incorrectly checked if the `readonly` flag was true, which would prevent write permissions from being set when they should have been. The fix corrected the condition to check if `readonly` is false, allowing the appropriate permissions to be granted and thus enabling the successful start of any domain.

    You will be given the root cause of a bug and  the corresponding patch.
    You need to extract the code statements that lead to the bug from  the patch, based on the root cause.

    
    Provide a response strictly in the following format:
    Code statements:
    <text1>
    <text2>

    <text4>
    ...
    <textN>

Root cause:
The bug was caused by a logic error in the permission check for cgroup device access, specifically in the condition that determines whether to set write permissions. The original code incorrectly checked if the `readonly` flag was true, which would prevent write permissions from being set when they should have been. The fix corrected the condition to check if `readonly` is false, allowing the appropriate permissions to be granted and thus enabling the successful start of any domain.
